text.assessment: The alert reports write latency and 5xx errors on inventory-service minutes after a deploy. Two independent lines of enquiry are worth opening: what the logs say failed first, and whether the numbers point at the database or at the service itself.
text.leading_hypothesis: Something in the database is blocking inventory-service writes.

questions.question: What is the earliest failure in the logs and what does it say caused it?
questions.why: Establishes the failure mode rather than the symptom.

questions.question: Which metrics are away from baseline, and is the service or the database the bottleneck?
questions.why: Separates a database cause from a compute or code one.

text.assessment: A root cause is established and grounded: the deploy's migration is building an index without CONCURRENTLY and its lock blocks every write. CPU is at baseline and replicas are healthy, which rules out compute and an outage.
text.leading_hypothesis: CREATE INDEX on stock_levels holds a lock that queues every write to the table.
